strongest_angle: Examines how nearly 4,000 nurses at Brigham and Women's Hospital postponed their planned strike after a grueling 13-hour marathon negotiation session and their 27th bargaining meeting.

key_facts.fact: Nearly 4,000 registered nurses at Brigham and Women's Hospital postponed their planned strike following a 13-hour bargaining session on Saturday.
The breakthrough occurred during the 27th bargaining session between hospital leadership and the Massachusetts Nurses Association.
The strike had been scheduled to begin just four days after the marathon negotiating session concluded with the hospital's final offer.
The unionized nurses at Mass General Brigham postponed what was set to be the largest open-ended nurse strike in Massachusetts history.
